Accepted registry record

A Foundation Model for Continuous Glucose Monitoring Data

2026 · Nature · model · Enabler · Cardiac & metabolic models

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Learns general representations from longitudinal continuous glucose monitoring data for multiple downstream metabolic tasks.
Why it matters
Expands reusable learning beyond one narrowly supervised endpoint and provides a reference point for cross-task, cross-dataset or label-efficient wearable modelling.
Limitations
Publication quality and pretraining scale do not establish cross-device, cross-cohort or clinical generalization; calibration, subgroup performance and deployment shift remain task-specific.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Signal pretraining and reusable representations support health estimation; a foundation model is not itself an individualized simulator or a proven intervention.

2026 · Nature Medicine · model · Research · Disease prediction

Disease risk · Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Pretrains across multimodal sleep-study signals and evaluates transfer to disease prediction, moving beyond sleep staging alone.
Why it matters
Expands reusable learning beyond one narrowly supervised endpoint and provides a reference point for cross-task, cross-dataset or label-efficient wearable modelling.
Limitations
Publication quality and pretraining scale do not establish cross-device, cross-cohort or clinical generalization; calibration, subgroup performance and deployment shift remain task-specific.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
The stated task is disease prediction from multimodal sleep signals; predictive evaluation does not demonstrate intervention effects or an individualized simulator.
Review note
Source scope: body-sensed-adjacent; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Daily Activity Patterns from Wearable Accelerometry Predict Physical Frailty and Concern about Falling

2026 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Uses free-living chest accelerometry and multi-task sequence modeling to jointly estimate frailty and concern about falling.
Why it matters
Illustrates how daily temporal organization and complexity may augment questionnaire-based geriatric assessment.
Limitations
The cohort is modest, measurements span only 48 hours, and reported discrimination requires external and prospective validation before screening use.
Evidence boundary
This supports analytical or clinical validation in the studied cohort and device setting; it does not establish universal cross-device validity or downstream clinical benefit.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

From Wrist Data to Lifespan: Elucidating Inflammation-Driven Biological Aging via Activity Rhythms Captured by Wearable Devices

2026 · npj Aging · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Evaluates wearable-derived activity rhythms in relation to inflammatory biological aging and lifespan-related outcomes.
Why it matters
Connects behavioral rhythm features with a plausible biological pathway and broadens wearable aging measurement beyond chronological-age prediction alone.
Limitations
Pathway analyses and longitudinal associations are vulnerable to residual confounding and do not prove that rhythm modification reverses biological aging.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

GlucoFM: A Foundation Model for Continuous Glucose Monitoring

2026 · Google Research · model · Enabler · Cardiac & metabolic models

Foundation models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Develops a glucose-focused foundation-model line for continuous glucose monitoring and downstream metabolic modelling.

Expands reusable learning beyond one narrowly supervised endpoint and provides a reference point for cross-task, cross-dataset or label-efficient wearable modelling.

Signal pretraining and reusable representations support health estimation; a foundation model is not itself an individualized simulator or a proven intervention.

High-Performance Self-Supervised Learning by Joint Training of Flow Matching

2026 · AISTATS · model · Enabler · Activity & behavior models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Introduces a flow-matching sensor foundation model that jointly learns representations and conditional generation on wearable sensor datasets.
Why it matters
Connects efficient generative modeling with reusable wearable representations and reports substantially faster training and inference than the diffusion comparator.
Limitations
Evidence is based on five downstream datasets and does not establish population-scale health transfer or clinical effectiveness.
Evidence boundary
This is representation-learning or predictive evidence. It does not establish that a sensor-derived prediction is a causal treatment effect, clinically useful decision rule, or safe deployed intervention.
Editorial placement
Wearable motion representations and activity recognition are upstream sensing capabilities, not causal treatment evidence or an implemented personal twin.

Longitudinal Digital Phenotyping of Activity Rhythms and Biological Aging Using Commercial Wearables

2026 · Nature Communications · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Links multi-year commercial wearable activity rhythms with longitudinal clinical biomarker-derived biological aging trajectories in All of Us participants.
Why it matters
Extends one-week cross-sectional digital aging work toward repeated, person-level trajectories using consumer devices and linked clinical biomarkers.
Limitations
The analysis remains observational, the linked sample is a subset of the cohort, and device-derived rhythm features may depend on wear patterns and proprietary preprocessing.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.

Accepted registry record

Sensor-Wide Association Studies in Digital Medicine

2026 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Framework · Biomarker evaluation frameworks

Biomarkers

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Proposes Sensor-Wide Association Studies for prespecified, multiplicity-controlled scans of sensor-derived features against clinical phenotypes.
Why it matters
Offers a transparent discovery framework for high-dimensional wearable feature libraries analogous to genome-wide association studies.
Limitations
The perspective defines a research design rather than proving that discovered sensor associations are causal, portable or clinically useful.
Evidence boundary
This is a methodological perspective; association discovery must be followed by replication, causal analysis and validation of intended use.
Editorial placement
A perspective or review organizes measurement and validation; it does not implement or validate a new patient-level predictive system.

Accepted registry record

TimesFM-3: A Zero-Shot Foundation Model for Multivariate Forecasting

2026 · Google Research · model · Enabler · General forecasting enablers

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Introduces a 330M-parameter multivariate zero-shot forecasting model pretrained on more than one trillion real and synthetic time points.
Why it matters
Provides a general time-series backbone or adaptation strategy that can be evaluated on wearable and physiological data without assuming modality-specific pretraining.
Limitations
The model was not developed specifically for wearable physiology; inclusion records transfer potential and benchmark relevance, not demonstrated wearable superiority.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
General time-series modelling is a transferable methodological resource; its inclusion does not demonstrate wearable disease prediction without a task-specific evaluation.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Transforming Wearable Data into Personal Health Insights Using Large Language Model Agents

2026 · Nature Communications · model · Enabler · Personal health interpretation

Foundation models · Personalization

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Evaluates an LLM-agent workflow that converts longitudinal wearable summaries and activity events into personal health analyses.
Why it matters
Connects sensor-derived evidence with natural-language reasoning, reporting, retrieval or interaction, a key interface layer for longitudinal wearable systems.
Limitations
Language outputs can be fluent while clinically wrong; grounding, calibration, privacy, hallucination control and prospective utility require independent evaluation.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Evaluates an agent workflow for analysing longitudinal wearable summaries; personal-data reasoning is a potential twin interface or analytical component, not an implemented individual digital twin.

Wearable Device Derived Electrocardiographic Age and Its Association with Atrial Fibrillation

2026 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Derives an AI electrocardiographic age measure from wearable-device ECG and evaluates its association with atrial fibrillation.
Why it matters
Extends ECG-age concepts from clinical 12-lead recordings to lower-burden wearable measurements.
Limitations
Association with AF does not establish incremental clinical utility, causal interpretation or transportability to other wearable ECG hardware.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Ambulatory Atrial Fibrillation Detection and Quantification by Wristworn AI Device Compared to Standard Holter Monitoring

2025 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease screening & monitoring

Biomarkers

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Compares wrist photoplethysmography and single-lead ECG algorithms with 24-hour Holter monitoring and extends observation for AF burden.
Why it matters
Evaluates both event detection and burden quantification, which is more clinically informative than a binary alert alone.
Limitations
The sample is limited, device-specific and enriched for evaluated patients; broader screening utility and effect on management require additional trials.
Evidence boundary
This supports analytical or clinical validation in the studied cohort and device setting; it does not establish universal cross-device validity or downstream clinical benefit.
Editorial placement
Rhythm detection and monitoring identify existing disease-related states; they are upstream evidence for the prediction route, not future disease forecasts or intervention-effect estimates.

Foundation models

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution

IMUZero: Zero-Shot Human Activity Recognition by Language-Based Cross-Modality Fusion

2025 · Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies · model · Enabler · Sensor-language & health reasoning

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Uses language-based cross-modal alignment to recognize activity classes without task-specific examples for every target label.
Why it matters
Extends wearable recognition beyond closed label sets and links IMU signals to semantic descriptions.
Limitations
Zero-shot activity recognition depends on label semantics and benchmark construction; it is not evidence of zero-shot disease diagnosis or causal reasoning.
Evidence boundary
This is representation-learning or predictive evidence. It does not establish that a sensor-derived prediction is a causal treatment effect, clinically useful decision rule, or safe deployed intervention.
Editorial placement
Grounding language in sensor observations supports interpretation of personal data; text alignment and fluent health reports are not validated intervention reasoning or personal twins.

LUNA: Efficient and Topology-Agnostic Foundation Model for EEG Signal Analysis

2025 · NeurIPS · model · Enabler · Brain, sleep & respiratory models

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Proposes an efficient topology-agnostic EEG foundation model intended to tolerate heterogeneous electrode layouts.
Why it matters
Expands reusable learning beyond one narrowly supervised endpoint and provides a reference point for cross-task, cross-dataset or label-efficient wearable modelling.
Limitations
Publication quality and pretraining scale do not establish cross-device, cross-cohort or clinical generalization; calibration, subgroup performance and deployment shift remain task-specific.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Representation learning supports physiological state analysis; transfer benchmarks do not alone establish prospective disease prediction or a personal twin.
Review note
Source scope: body-sensed-adjacent; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

MIRA: Medical Time Series Foundation Model for Real-World Health Data

2025 · NeurIPS · model · Enabler · General forecasting enablers

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Develops a continuous-time medical time-series foundation model pretrained on a heterogeneous corpus reported to contain more than 454 billion time points.
Why it matters
Its treatment of irregular intervals, heterogeneous sampling and missingness is relevant to longitudinal wearable-health streams even though the paper is not wearable-specific.
Limitations
The primary focus is medical forecasting rather than raw wearable sensing; transfer to free-living consumer devices requires direct evaluation.
Evidence boundary
This is representation-learning or predictive evidence. It does not establish that a sensor-derived prediction is a causal treatment effect, clinically useful decision rule, or safe deployed intervention.
Editorial placement
General time-series modelling is a transferable methodological resource; its inclusion does not demonstrate wearable disease prediction without a task-specific evaluation.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

MoPFormer: Motion-Primitive Transformer for Wearable-Sensor Activity Recognition

2025 · NeurIPS · model · Enabler · Activity & behavior models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Tokenizes IMU streams into discrete motion primitives and pretrains a masked-motion transformer evaluated on six HAR benchmarks and cross-dataset transfer.
Why it matters
Provides an interpretable discrete vocabulary for motion and explicitly evaluates cross-dataset generalization.
Limitations
Evaluation remains concentrated on activity-recognition benchmarks; robustness to long-duration free-living health prediction and unseen devices is not established.
Evidence boundary
This is representation-learning or predictive evidence. It does not establish that a sensor-derived prediction is a causal treatment effect, clinically useful decision rule, or safe deployed intervention.
Editorial placement
Wearable motion representations and activity recognition are upstream sensing capabilities, not causal treatment evidence or an implemented personal twin.

One Model to Fit Them All: Universal IMU-based Human Activity Recognition with LLM-assisted Cross-dataset Representation

2025 · Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies · model · Enabler · Sensor-language & health reasoning

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Constructs an LLM-assisted representation intended to support a single IMU activity-recognition model across heterogeneous datasets.
Why it matters
Directly addresses incompatible activity taxonomies and acquisition settings across wearable HAR datasets.
Limitations
Universality is bounded by the included datasets, sensor channels and label ontology; disease and intervention generalization were not evaluated.
Evidence boundary
This is representation-learning or predictive evidence. It does not establish that a sensor-derived prediction is a causal treatment effect, clinically useful decision rule, or safe deployed intervention.
Editorial placement
Grounding language in sensor observations supports interpretation of personal data; text alignment and fluent health reports are not validated intervention reasoning or personal twins.

Reading Your Heart: Learning ECG Words and Sentences via Pre-training ECG Language Model

2025 · ICLR · model · Enabler · Cardiac & metabolic models

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Tokenizes ECG morphology into word- and sentence-like structures for transferable cardiac representation learning.
Why it matters
Expands reusable learning beyond one narrowly supervised endpoint and provides a reference point for cross-task, cross-dataset or label-efficient wearable modelling.
Limitations
Publication quality and pretraining scale do not establish cross-device, cross-cohort or clinical generalization; calibration, subgroup performance and deployment shift remain task-specific.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Signal pretraining and reusable representations support health estimation; a foundation model is not itself an individualized simulator or a proven intervention.
Review note
Source scope: body-sensed-adjacent; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

REVE: A Foundation Model for EEG - Adapting to Any Setup with Large-Scale Pretraining on 25,000 Subjects

2025 · NeurIPS · model · Enabler · Brain, sleep & respiratory models

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Pretrains a topology-flexible EEG foundation model on more than 60,000 hours from 92 datasets and approximately 25,000 subjects, then evaluates transfer across ten EEG tasks.
Why it matters
Directly addresses electrode-layout, dataset and protocol heterogeneity, a central obstacle to reusable EEG representations.
Limitations
Reported transfer is limited to the evaluated EEG corpora and tasks; clinical utility, demographic robustness and prospective deployment were not established by the conference study.
Evidence boundary
This is representation-learning or predictive evidence. It does not establish that a sensor-derived prediction is a causal treatment effect, clinically useful decision rule, or safe deployed intervention.
Editorial placement
Representation learning supports physiological state analysis; transfer benchmarks do not alone establish prospective disease prediction or a personal twin.
Review note
Source scope: body-sensed-adjacent; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

SEMPO: Lightweight Foundation Models for Time Series Forecasting

2025 · NeurIPS · model · Enabler · General forecasting enablers

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Develops a lightweight spectral and prompt-mixture foundation model for zero- and few-shot time-series forecasting.
Why it matters
Its focus on model and data efficiency is relevant to wearable and edge settings where foundation-model cost is a limiting factor.
Limitations
The reported benchmarks are general forecasting datasets; wearable physiological validity must be demonstrated separately.
Evidence boundary
This is representation-learning or predictive evidence. It does not establish that a sensor-derived prediction is a causal treatment effect, clinically useful decision rule, or safe deployed intervention.
Editorial placement
General time-series modelling is a transferable methodological resource; its inclusion does not demonstrate wearable disease prediction without a task-specific evaluation.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

SensorLM: Learning the Language of Wearable Sensors

2025 · NeurIPS · model · Enabler · Sensor-language & health reasoning

Foundation models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Aligns wearable sensor sequences with language to support semantically grounded reasoning and transfer over human sensing data.
Why it matters
Connects sensor-derived evidence with natural-language reasoning, reporting, retrieval or interaction, a key interface layer for longitudinal wearable systems.
Limitations
Language outputs can be fluent while clinically wrong; grounding, calibration, privacy, hallucination control and prospective utility require independent evaluation.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Grounding language in sensor observations supports interpretation of personal data; text alignment and fluent health reports are not validated intervention reasoning or personal twins.

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Uses prior-data-fitted-network training on synthetic processes for zero-shot multivariate forecasting.

Towards a Personal Health Large Language Model

2025 · Nature Medicine · model · Enabler · Personal health interpretation

Foundation models · Personalization

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Studies LLM adaptation and evaluation for personalized reasoning over longitudinal wearable health data and expert-authored tasks.
Why it matters
Connects sensor-derived evidence with natural-language reasoning, reporting, retrieval or interaction, a key interface layer for longitudinal wearable systems.
Limitations
Language outputs can be fluent while clinically wrong; grounding, calibration, privacy, hallucination control and prospective utility require independent evaluation.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Studies language-model adaptation and evaluation for reasoning over personal wearable data; personalized health language does not establish causal intervention effects or a dynamic personal twin.
Review note
Source identity requires review: the registry retains a preprint-style title and journal URL that may not identify the corresponding final sleep-and-fitness-coaching paper. No canonical metadata is changed here.

WatchSleepNet: A Novel Model and Pretraining Approach for Advancing Sleep Staging with Smartwatches

2025 · CHIL · model · Enabler · Brain, sleep & respiratory models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Introduces an open smartwatch-oriented sleep-staging pipeline with a staged pretraining design and evaluates it on consumer-wearable signals.
Why it matters
Connects sleep representation learning to deployable wrist sensing, where signal availability and noise differ substantially from full polysomnography.
Limitations
Sleep-stage labels and performance remain dataset-, device- and population-dependent; comparison with clinical polysomnography does not establish diagnostic equivalence.
Evidence boundary
This record supports a representation, recognition, sensing or control-system claim under the reported evaluation. It does not by itself establish clinical benefit, causal treatment effect, safety, transportability or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Representation learning supports physiological state analysis; transfer benchmarks do not alone establish prospective disease prediction or a personal twin.

Wearable Data Reveals Distinct Characteristics of Individuals with Persistent Symptoms after a SARS-CoV-2 Infection

2025 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Identifies pre- and post-infection behavioral and physiological characteristics associated with persistent fatigue and dyspnea.
Why it matters
Shows why pre-event wearable baselines matter when interpreting post-viral trajectories and potential risk markers.
Limitations
The persistent-symptom subgroup was small and pre-existing differences limit claims that infection caused the observed digital phenotype.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata

Association of Physical Activity Pattern and Risk of Parkinson’s Disease

2024 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Compares concentrated weekend-warrior and regularly distributed accelerometer-derived activity patterns with incident Parkinson disease.
Why it matters
Adds temporal distribution of activity to total-volume digital epidemiology.
Limitations
Activity pattern is observational, incident cases are relatively few, and undiagnosed prodromal disease could influence behavior.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Circadian Rhythm Analysis Using Wearable-Based Accelerometry as a Digital Biomarker of Aging and Healthspan

2024 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Research · Aging & outcome risk estimation

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Introduces CosinorAge from seven-day wrist accelerometry and evaluates mortality, incident disease and functional outcomes across UK and US cohorts.
Why it matters
Provides an interpretable example of converting rest–activity rhythm intensity, phase and timing into an externally evaluated digital aging measure.
Limitations
The measurement window was limited, cohorts differed in device placement, and UK Biobank is healthier and less diverse than the general population.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.
Editorial placement
Evaluates a wearable circadian aging measure against mortality and incident disease outcomes across cohorts; outcome associations do not identify the effect of altering the circadian measure.

CrossHAR: Generalizing Cross-Dataset Human Activity Recognition via Hierarchical Self-Supervised Pretraining

2024 · Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies · model · Enabler · Activity & behavior models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Develops hierarchical self-supervised pretraining for cross-dataset activity recognition under heterogeneous sensor and label conditions.
Why it matters
Provides a directly relevant benchmark point for evaluating whether wearable representations transfer beyond a single curated dataset.
Limitations
Transfer remains constrained by overlap in activities, devices, placements and population characteristics, and does not imply universal zero-shot recognition.
Evidence boundary
This record supports a representation, recognition, sensing or control-system claim under the reported evaluation. It does not by itself establish clinical benefit, causal treatment effect, safety, transportability or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Wearable motion representations and activity recognition are upstream sensing capabilities, not causal treatment evidence or an implemented personal twin.

General Time Transformer: An Encoder-Decoder Foundation Model for Most Time Series Analysis Tasks

2024 · CIKM · model · Enabler · General forecasting enablers

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Builds an encoder-decoder foundation model intended to span several time-series analysis tasks.
Why it matters
Provides a general time-series backbone or adaptation strategy that can be evaluated on wearable and physiological data without assuming modality-specific pretraining.
Limitations
The model was not developed specifically for wearable physiology; inclusion records transfer potential and benchmark relevance, not demonstrated wearable superiority.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
General time-series modelling is a transferable methodological resource; its inclusion does not demonstrate wearable disease prediction without a task-specific evaluation.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

GOAT: A Generalized Cross-Dataset Activity Recognition Framework with Natural Language Supervision

2024 · Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies · model · Enabler · Activity & behavior models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Uses natural-language supervision to align heterogeneous activity label spaces and improve cross-dataset wearable activity recognition.
Why it matters
Addresses semantic incompatibility across HAR datasets, a major obstacle to reusable sensor models and foundation-model evaluation.
Limitations
Generalization is bounded by the selected datasets, label descriptions, sensor placements and activity ontologies; language supervision does not remove domain shift.
Evidence boundary
This record supports a representation, recognition, sensing or control-system claim under the reported evaluation. It does not by itself establish clinical benefit, causal treatment effect, safety, transportability or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Wearable motion representations and activity recognition are upstream sensing capabilities, not causal treatment evidence or an implemented personal twin.

Integrating Large Language Models, EEG, and Eye Tracking for Word-Level Neural State Classification in Reading Comprehension

2024 · IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering · model · Enabler · Neural-state estimation

Foundation models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Integrates EEG, eye tracking and language-model representations for word-level neural-state classification.
Why it matters
Connects sensor-derived evidence with natural-language reasoning, reporting, retrieval or interaction, a key interface layer for longitudinal wearable systems.
Limitations
Language outputs can be fluent while clinically wrong; grounding, calibration, privacy, hallucination control and prospective utility require independent evaluation.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Classifies word-level neural states during reading using EEG, eye tracking, and language representations; eye tracking alone does not make this a mixed-reality input system.
Review note
Source scope: body-sensed-adjacent; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Large-Scale Training of Foundation Models for Wearable Biosignals

2024 · ICLR · model · Enabler · Multimodal physiological models

Foundation models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Evaluates large-scale pretraining for wearable ECG and PPG representations across downstream tasks.
Why it matters
Expands reusable learning beyond one narrowly supervised endpoint and provides a reference point for cross-task, cross-dataset or label-efficient wearable modelling.
Limitations
Publication quality and pretraining scale do not establish cross-device, cross-cohort or clinical generalization; calibration, subgroup performance and deployment shift remain task-specific.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Multisignal representation learning supports health-state estimation; fusion or personalization alone does not establish a dynamic personal twin.

Long-term Changes in Wearable Sensor Data in People with and without Long Covid

2024 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Compares step count, resting heart rate and sleep trajectories for up to one year after infection in participants with and without Long COVID.
Why it matters
Illustrates person-specific recovery curves and persistent deviations that episodic clinic visits can miss.
Limitations
Long COVID was self-reported, groups differed at baseline, and trajectories cannot by themselves identify mechanisms or treatment effects.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Scaling Wearable Foundation Models

2024 · Google Research · model · Enabler · Multimodal physiological models

Foundation models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Studies data and model scaling for multimodal wearable foundation models using tens of millions of hours from more than 165,000 participants.
Why it matters
Expands reusable learning beyond one narrowly supervised endpoint and provides a reference point for cross-task, cross-dataset or label-efficient wearable modelling.
Limitations
Publication quality and pretraining scale do not establish cross-device, cross-cohort or clinical generalization; calibration, subgroup performance and deployment shift remain task-specific.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Multisignal representation learning supports health-state estimation; fusion or personalization alone does not establish a dynamic personal twin.

Self-Supervised Learning of Accelerometer Data Provides New Insights for Sleep and Its Association with Mortality

2024 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Develops accelerometer-based sleep classification and applies derived sleep duration and efficiency measures to mortality analyses in UK Biobank.
Why it matters
Links representation learning, digital sleep measurement and population outcomes in a single reproducible pipeline.
Limitations
Agreement with polysomnography is only fair to moderate and mortality analyses remain observational with a single baseline wear period.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Sensor2Text: Enabling Natural Language Interactions for Daily Activity Tracking Using Wearable Sensors

2024 · Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies · model · Enabler · Sensor-language & health reasoning

Foundation models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Translates wearable sensor observations into language-oriented representations for interactive daily-activity tracking.
Why it matters
Connects sensor-derived evidence with natural-language reasoning, reporting, retrieval or interaction, a key interface layer for longitudinal wearable systems.
Limitations
Language outputs can be fluent while clinically wrong; grounding, calibration, privacy, hallucination control and prospective utility require independent evaluation.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Maps wearable activity observations to language for interactive tracking; descriptive language interaction does not demonstrate a metaverse entry or dynamic personal twin.

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Pretrains a Siamese convolutional model for transferable PPG signal-quality and representation tasks.

Signal pretraining and reusable representations support health estimation; a foundation model is not itself an individualized simulator or a proven intervention.

SleepFM: Multi-modal Representation Learning for Sleep Across Brain Activity, ECG and Respiratory Signals

2024 · ICML · model · Enabler · Brain, sleep & respiratory models

Foundation models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Pretrains a multimodal sleep representation model on more than 100,000 hours of polysomnography from over 14,000 participants and evaluates transfer to sleep-related tasks.
Why it matters
Establishes a large-scale, cross-modal reference for learning from brain, cardiac and respiratory sleep signals rather than treating each channel in isolation.
Limitations
The source data are laboratory or clinical polysomnography rather than everyday smartwatch sensing, and reported downstream gains do not establish prospective diagnostic utility.
Evidence boundary
This record supports a representation, recognition, sensing or control-system claim under the reported evaluation. It does not by itself establish clinical benefit, causal treatment effect, safety, transportability or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Representation learning supports physiological state analysis; transfer benchmarks do not alone establish prospective disease prediction or a personal twin.

Temporally Multi-Scale Sparse Self-Attention for Physical Activity Data Imputation

2024 · CHIL · method · Enabler · Signal quality & trustworthy models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Develops multi-scale sparse attention for imputing large-scale hourly step-count series with realistic wearable missingness.
Why it matters
Addresses non-wear, irregular observation, device error and missingness mechanisms that otherwise contaminate wearable phenotypes and downstream causal analyses.
Limitations
Imputation or calibration can conceal non-random missingness and device-specific failure; uncertainty and sensitivity analyses remain necessary.
Evidence boundary
Improved reconstruction or calibration does not establish that downstream biological or treatment-effect conclusions are unbiased.
Editorial placement
Calibration, missing-data handling, privacy, and bias analysis support reliable wearable measurements and models; these methods do not themselves achieve a clinical endpoint.

2024 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Derives wearable-based circadian misalignment measures and relates them bidirectionally to mood in medical interns undergoing shift-work transition.
Why it matters
Shows how multiple internal rhythms and sleep timing can be combined into interpretable longitudinal mental-health markers.
Limitations
The cohort is occupation-specific and observational; bidirectional associations and time-varying confounding limit causal interpretation.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.

Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Time-LLM: Time Series Forecasting by Reprogramming Large Language Models

2024 · ICLR · model · Enabler · General forecasting enablers

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Reprograms frozen large language models for time-series forecasting through prototype and prompt alignment.
Why it matters
Provides a general time-series backbone or adaptation strategy that can be evaluated on wearable and physiological data without assuming modality-specific pretraining.
Limitations
The model was not developed specifically for wearable physiology; inclusion records transfer potential and benchmark relevance, not demonstrated wearable superiority.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
General time-series modelling is a transferable methodological resource; its inclusion does not demonstrate wearable disease prediction without a task-specific evaluation.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Towards Open Respiratory Acoustic Foundation Models: Pretraining and Benchmarking

2024 · NeurIPS · model · Enabler · Brain, sleep & respiratory models

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Builds and benchmarks open respiratory acoustic representations across multiple respiratory-sound tasks.
Why it matters
Expands reusable learning beyond one narrowly supervised endpoint and provides a reference point for cross-task, cross-dataset or label-efficient wearable modelling.
Limitations
Publication quality and pretraining scale do not establish cross-device, cross-cohort or clinical generalization; calibration, subgroup performance and deployment shift remain task-specific.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Representation learning supports physiological state analysis; transfer benchmarks do not alone establish prospective disease prediction or a personal twin.
Review note
Source scope: body-sensed-adjacent; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

UniMTS: Unified Pre-training for Motion Time Series

2024 · NeurIPS · model · Enabler · Activity & behavior models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Develops unified pretraining for heterogeneous motion time series and evaluates transfer across motion-sensing tasks and configurations.
Why it matters
Targets sensor-, position- and task-level heterogeneity that limits reusable IMU models.
Limitations
The conference evaluation does not establish generality to all wearable devices, very long free-living recordings or clinical outcomes.
Evidence boundary
This is representation-learning or predictive evidence. It does not establish that a sensor-derived prediction is a causal treatment effect, clinically useful decision rule, or safe deployed intervention.
Editorial placement
Wearable motion representations and activity recognition are upstream sensing capabilities, not causal treatment evidence or an implemented personal twin.

UniTS: Building a Unified Time Series Model

2024 · NeurIPS · model · Enabler · General forecasting enablers

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Unifies forecasting, classification, imputation and anomaly detection in one time-series model.
Why it matters
Provides a general time-series backbone or adaptation strategy that can be evaluated on wearable and physiological data without assuming modality-specific pretraining.
Limitations
The model was not developed specifically for wearable physiology; inclusion records transfer potential and benchmark relevance, not demonstrated wearable superiority.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
General time-series modelling is a transferable methodological resource; its inclusion does not demonstrate wearable disease prediction without a task-specific evaluation.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Association of Accelerometer-Measured Physical Activity Intensity, Sedentary Time, and Exercise Time with Incident Parkinson’s Disease

2023 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Relates accelerometer-derived activity intensity, sedentary time and exercise timing to incident Parkinson disease in UK Biobank.
Why it matters
Uses objective free-living movement measures to examine timing and composition of activity in relation to future neurological diagnosis.
Limitations
Prodromal disease and reverse causation are plausible, and observational associations do not prove preventive effects of exercise prescriptions.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Accepted registry record

BIOT: Biosignal Transformer for Cross-Data Learning in the Wild

2023 · NeurIPS · model · Enabler · Multimodal physiological models

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Introduces a transformer for cross-dataset learning over heterogeneous biosignals collected in real-world settings.
Why it matters
Expands reusable learning beyond one narrowly supervised endpoint and provides a reference point for cross-task, cross-dataset or label-efficient wearable modelling.
Limitations
Publication quality and pretraining scale do not establish cross-device, cross-cohort or clinical generalization; calibration, subgroup performance and deployment shift remain task-specific.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Multisignal representation learning supports health-state estimation; fusion or personalization alone does not establish a dynamic personal twin.
Review note
Source scope: body-sensed-adjacent; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

One Fits All: Power General Time Series Analysis by Pretrained Language Model

2023 · NeurIPS · model · Enabler · General forecasting enablers

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Adapts pretrained language models to multiple time-series tasks through a shared representation interface.
Why it matters
Provides a general time-series backbone or adaptation strategy that can be evaluated on wearable and physiological data without assuming modality-specific pretraining.
Limitations
The model was not developed specifically for wearable physiology; inclusion records transfer potential and benchmark relevance, not demonstrated wearable superiority.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
General time-series modelling is a transferable methodological resource; its inclusion does not demonstrate wearable disease prediction without a task-specific evaluation.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

ColloSSL: Collaborative Self-Supervised Learning for Human Activity Recognition

2022 · Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies · model · Enabler · Activity & behavior models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Uses synchronized signals from multiple wearable devices as natural supervision for self-supervised activity representation learning.
Why it matters
Shows how cross-device co-occurrence can supply supervision without manual labels and motivates multi-device pretraining strategies.
Limitations
The method assumes access to collaborative or synchronized devices during pretraining and its transfer depends on sensor configuration and task similarity.
Evidence boundary
This record supports a representation, recognition, sensing or control-system claim under the reported evaluation. It does not by itself establish clinical benefit, causal treatment effect, safety, transportability or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Wearable motion representations and activity recognition are upstream sensing capabilities, not causal treatment evidence or an implemented personal twin.

Detection of Atrial Fibrillation in a Large Population Using Wearable Devices: The Fitbit Heart Study

2022 · Circulation · measure · Enabler · Disease screening & monitoring

Biomarkers

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Prospectively evaluates a wearable photoplethysmography irregular-rhythm algorithm with confirmatory ECG patch monitoring at population scale.
Why it matters
Complements smartwatch notification studies by testing a different commercial ecosystem and continuous pulse-tachogram pipeline.
Limitations
The study is enriched by digital recruitment and confirmation occurs after notification, so sensitivity and clinical outcome effects are not established.
Evidence boundary
This supports analytical or clinical validation in the studied cohort and device setting; it does not establish universal cross-device validity or downstream clinical benefit.
Editorial placement
Rhythm detection and monitoring identify existing disease-related states; they are upstream evidence for the prediction route, not future disease forecasts or intervention-effect estimates.

Accepted registry record

Prospective Associations of Daily Step Counts and Intensity With Cancer and Cardiovascular Disease Incidence and Mortality and All-Cause Mortality

2022 · JAMA Internal Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Assesses daily step volume and peak cadence against cancer, cardiovascular disease and mortality outcomes in 78,500 UK Biobank participants.
Why it matters
Provides dose-response evidence for an intuitive wearable measure across several public-health endpoints.
Limitations
The cohort is predominantly White, step exposure is based on a limited wear period, and observed associations do not prove benefits of prescribed step targets.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

TS2Vec: Towards Universal Representation of Time Series

2022 · AAAI · model · Enabler · General forecasting enablers

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Learns hierarchical contrastive time-series representations that are widely used as a transferable baseline for sensor data.
Why it matters
Provides a general time-series backbone or adaptation strategy that can be evaluated on wearable and physiological data without assuming modality-specific pretraining.
Limitations
The model was not developed specifically for wearable physiology; inclusion records transfer potential and benchmark relevance, not demonstrated wearable superiority.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
General time-series modelling is a transferable methodological resource; its inclusion does not demonstrate wearable disease prediction without a task-specific evaluation.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Virtual Exam for Parkinson’s Disease Enables Frequent and Reliable Remote Measurements of Motor Function

2022 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Validates smartwatch-based unsupervised motor tasks for tremor, bradykinesia and gait over long-term remote follow-up.
Why it matters
Demonstrates reliability, medication sensitivity and sustained engagement for repeated digital motor outcomes.
Limitations
The code is proprietary, active tasks require adherence, and validity was established in early-stage Parkinson disease using a specific watch.
Evidence boundary
This supports analytical or clinical validation in the studied cohort and device setting; it does not establish universal cross-device validity or downstream clinical benefit.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Accepted registry record

Wearable Accelerometer-Derived Physical Activity and Incident Disease

2022 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Tests accelerometer-derived moderate-to-vigorous physical activity against 697 incident disease outcomes in 96,244 UK Biobank participants.
Why it matters
Demonstrates the breadth of phenome-wide association possible with standardized wearable activity measures and linked longitudinal health records.
Limitations
One-week exposure measurement, selection into UK Biobank, multiple testing and residual confounding limit causal interpretation and individual risk use.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

actipy

2021 · Canonical project documentation · infrastructure · Enabler · Tools, platforms & evaluation

Original source · Code · Project

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Python toolkit for reading, calibrating, resampling and summarizing raw wearable accelerometry.
Why it matters
Supports transparent preprocessing and cross-device workflows for large accelerometer datasets.
Limitations
Harmonized preprocessing cannot remove all hardware, placement and protocol differences.
Evidence boundary
Tool inclusion documents available research infrastructure; it does not validate downstream scientific, causal or clinical claims.

BENDR: Using Transformers and a Contrastive Self-Supervised Learning Task to Learn from Massive Amounts of EEG Data

2021 · Frontiers in Human Neuroscience · model · Enabler · Brain, sleep & respiratory models

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Applies transformer-based contrastive self-supervision to large EEG collections for downstream transfer.
Why it matters
Expands reusable learning beyond one narrowly supervised endpoint and provides a reference point for cross-task, cross-dataset or label-efficient wearable modelling.
Limitations
Publication quality and pretraining scale do not establish cross-device, cross-cohort or clinical generalization; calibration, subgroup performance and deployment shift remain task-specific.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Representation learning supports physiological state analysis; transfer benchmarks do not alone establish prospective disease prediction or a personal twin.
Review note
Source scope: body-sensed-adjacent; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Passive Detection of COVID-19 with Wearable Sensors and Explainable Machine Learning Algorithms

2021 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Builds an explainable wearable-based COVID-19 detection model that can operate with missing symptoms and heterogeneous available sensor streams.
Why it matters
Addresses deployment realities such as incomplete self-report and variable consumer devices.
Limitations
Predictive performance declines when restricted to pre-test passive data, and prospective alert utility and false-positive burden require evaluation.
Evidence boundary
This supports analytical or clinical validation in the studied cohort and device setting; it does not establish universal cross-device validity or downstream clinical benefit.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Evaluates whether wrist- and waist-wearable activity patterns improve prediction of changes in HbA1c among adults with prediabetes.

Connects free-living behavior to a clinically familiar metabolic outcome and explicitly compares wearable placement.

The analysis predicts change within a trial cohort but does not establish that model-guided behavior change improves glycemic control.

Accepted registry record

Unsupervised Representation Learning for Time Series with Temporal Neighborhood Coding

2021 · ICLR · model · Enabler · General forecasting enablers

Foundation models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Defines temporal neighborhoods for unsupervised representation learning and is frequently applicable to wearable time series.
Why it matters
Provides a general time-series backbone or adaptation strategy that can be evaluated on wearable and physiological data without assuming modality-specific pretraining.
Limitations
The model was not developed specifically for wearable physiology; inclusion records transfer potential and benchmark relevance, not demonstrated wearable superiority.
Evidence boundary
This is representation or predictive-model evidence. It does not by itself establish a causal treatment effect, clinical benefit, safety, or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
General time-series modelling is a transferable methodological resource; its inclusion does not demonstrate wearable disease prediction without a task-specific evaluation.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Wearable Sensor Data and Self-Reported Symptoms for COVID-19 Detection

2021 · Nature Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Combines longitudinal wearable data with symptoms to distinguish symptomatic COVID-19 positive and negative participants.
Why it matters
Shows complementary information from passive sensing and self-report in a large remotely recruited study.
Limitations
The number of test-positive symptomatic participants used for modeling was limited and the result does not replace diagnostic testing.
Evidence boundary
This supports analytical or clinical validation in the studied cohort and device setting; it does not establish universal cross-device validity or downstream clinical benefit.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Association of Daily Step Count and Step Intensity With Mortality Among US Adults

2020 · JAMA · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Relates accelerometer-measured daily steps and cadence to all-cause, cardiovascular and cancer mortality in a nationally representative US cohort.
Why it matters
Anchors widely used step-count measures to long-term outcomes and separates total volume from intensity.
Limitations
The exposure was measured once for up to seven days and the observational design cannot identify an intervention target or eliminate reverse causation.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Accepted registry record

Investigating Sources of Inaccuracy in Wearable Optical Heart Rate Sensors

2020 · npj Digital Medicine · method · Enabler · Signal quality & trustworthy models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Evaluates device, activity and participant-related error sources in consumer optical heart-rate sensors.
Why it matters
Addresses non-wear, irregular observation, device error and missingness mechanisms that otherwise contaminate wearable phenotypes and downstream causal analyses.
Limitations
Imputation or calibration can conceal non-random missingness and device-specific failure; uncertainty and sensitivity analyses remain necessary.
Evidence boundary
Improved reconstruction or calibration does not establish that downstream biological or treatment-effect conclusions are unbiased.
Editorial placement
Calibration, missing-data handling, privacy, and bias analysis support reliable wearable measurements and models; these methods do not themselves achieve a clinical endpoint.

Accepted registry record

Multi-task Deep Learning for Cardiac Rhythm Detection in Wearable Devices

2020 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease screening & monitoring

Biomarkers

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Jointly models photoplethysmography signal quality and atrial-fibrillation detection with transfer learning and a prospective replication cohort.
Why it matters
Treats signal quality as part of the clinical measurement problem rather than assuming all wearable pulse windows are usable.
Limitations
Evaluation remains device- and cohort-dependent, and algorithmic accuracy does not establish improved diagnosis, treatment or outcomes.
Evidence boundary
This supports analytical or clinical validation in the studied cohort and device setting; it does not establish universal cross-device validity or downstream clinical benefit.
Editorial placement
Rhythm detection and monitoring identify existing disease-related states; they are upstream evidence for the prediction route, not future disease forecasts or intervention-effect estimates.

Accepted registry record

Pre-symptomatic Detection of COVID-19 from Smartwatch Data

2020 · Nature Biomedical Engineering · measure · Research · Early disease warning

Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Uses individualized deviations in heart rate, steps and sleep to identify physiological changes around COVID-19 and other illnesses.
Why it matters
Demonstrates the value of personal baselines for detecting acute deviations before or near symptom onset.
Limitations
The number of confirmed cases was small, analyses were largely retrospective, and alert specificity across other stressors and infections remains challenging.
Evidence boundary
This supports analytical or clinical validation in the studied cohort and device setting; it does not establish universal cross-device validity or downstream clinical benefit.
Editorial placement
Uses deviations from an individual's wearable baseline to detect changes around infection; early warning and baseline personalization do not establish a dynamic twin or causal treatment effect.

Digital Assessment of Falls Risk, Frailty, and Mobility Impairment Using Wearable Sensors

2019 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Evaluates sensor-derived mobility features for classifying falls risk, frailty and mobility impairment.
Why it matters
Provides an early integrated digital-measure framework across related geriatric outcomes rather than a single laboratory gait variable.
Limitations
Performance depends on cohort composition and test protocol, and classification evidence is not equivalent to prospective fall prevention or clinical utility.
Evidence boundary
This supports analytical or clinical validation in the studied cohort and device setting; it does not establish universal cross-device validity or downstream clinical benefit.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Accepted registry record

Dissecting Racial Bias in an Algorithm Used to Manage the Health of Populations

2019 · Science · method · Enabler · Signal quality & trustworthy models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Shows how a cost-based proxy produced substantial racial bias in population-health risk stratification.
Why it matters
Supports privacy, fairness or transportability requirements for population-scale wearable AI and multi-institutional learning.
Limitations
Formal privacy or fairness guarantees cover specific threat models and metrics; they do not guarantee equitable clinical benefit across all populations.
Evidence boundary
Governance-oriented methodology must be evaluated in the intended population and deployment context before clinical claims are made.
Editorial placement
Calibration, missing-data handling, privacy, and bias analysis support reliable wearable measurements and models; these methods do not themselves achieve a clinical endpoint.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Large-Scale Assessment of a Smartwatch to Identify Atrial Fibrillation

2019 · New England Journal of Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease screening & monitoring

Biomarkers

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Evaluates smartwatch irregular-pulse notifications followed by telemedicine and ambulatory ECG confirmation in 419,297 participants.
Why it matters
Provides population-scale prospective evidence on notification yield and positive predictive value in real-world smartwatch use.
Limitations
Enrollment was self-selected, only notified participants received confirmatory monitoring, and the design did not estimate population sensitivity or outcome benefit.
Evidence boundary
This supports analytical or clinical validation in the studied cohort and device setting; it does not establish universal cross-device validity or downstream clinical benefit.
Editorial placement
Rhythm detection and monitoring identify existing disease-related states; they are upstream evidence for the prediction route, not future disease forecasts or intervention-effect estimates.

Accepted registry record

BRITS: Bidirectional Recurrent Imputation for Time Series

2018 · NeurIPS · method · Enabler · Signal quality & trustworthy models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Treats missing values as trainable variables in a bidirectional recurrent imputation model.
Why it matters
Addresses non-wear, irregular observation, device error and missingness mechanisms that otherwise contaminate wearable phenotypes and downstream causal analyses.
Limitations
Imputation or calibration can conceal non-random missingness and device-specific failure; uncertainty and sensitivity analyses remain necessary.
Evidence boundary
Improved reconstruction or calibration does not establish that downstream biological or treatment-effect conclusions are unbiased.
Editorial placement
Calibration, missing-data handling, privacy, and bias analysis support reliable wearable measurements and models; these methods do not themselves achieve a clinical endpoint.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

2018 · Official dataset resource · dataset · Enabler · Datasets & longitudinal cohorts

Original source · Data

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Open sleep datasets supporting comparison between wearable headband signals and polysomnography.
Why it matters
Supports reproducible model development, cross-dataset comparison, external validation or population-scale wearable epidemiology with explicit acquisition and access metadata.
Limitations
Official availability does not imply harmonized labels, devices, sampling rates, licensing or population representativeness; users must inspect the current data dictionary and access terms.
Evidence boundary
Dataset inclusion documents research infrastructure. It does not validate any model, clinical claim, treatment effect or cross-device generalization result.
Editorial placement
A dataset or cohort provides sensing and evaluation infrastructure; its availability is not evidence that a predictive, causal, or twin capability has been achieved.

Accepted registry record

Large-Scale Wearable Data Reveal Digital Phenotypes for Daily-Life Stress Detection

2018 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Analyzes five days of free-living wearable physiology, context and self-report from 1,002 participants to characterize daily-life stress phenotypes.
Why it matters
Demonstrates why ambulatory stress models require personalization and population-scale heterogeneity rather than laboratory signals alone.
Limitations
Stress labels are self-reported, the study is cross-sectional, and physiological response may reflect many non-stress processes.
Evidence boundary
The reported relationship is observational or predictive. It does not establish that changing the wearable-derived measure will causally change the clinical outcome.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Accepted registry record

Passive Detection of Atrial Fibrillation Using a Commercially Available Smartwatch

2018 · JAMA Cardiology · measure · Enabler · Disease screening & monitoring

Biomarkers

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Trains and externally tests a deep neural network on commercial smartwatch photoplethysmography for passive atrial-fibrillation detection.
Why it matters
Established an early proof of concept for longitudinal rhythm inference from commodity wearable pulse data.
Limitations
Performance fell in ambulatory self-reported analysis, the external criterion-standard cohort was small, and prospective screening utility was not demonstrated.
Evidence boundary
This supports analytical or clinical validation in the studied cohort and device setting; it does not establish universal cross-device validity or downstream clinical benefit.
Editorial placement
Rhythm detection and monitoring identify existing disease-related states; they are upstream evidence for the prediction route, not future disease forecasts or intervention-effect estimates.

Accepted registry record

Recurrent Neural Networks for Multivariate Time Series with Missing Values

2018 · Scientific Reports · method · Enabler · Signal quality & trustworthy models

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Introduces GRU-D, incorporating masks and time gaps to model informative missingness in multivariate clinical time series.
Why it matters
Addresses non-wear, irregular observation, device error and missingness mechanisms that otherwise contaminate wearable phenotypes and downstream causal analyses.
Limitations
Imputation or calibration can conceal non-random missingness and device-specific failure; uncertainty and sensitivity analyses remain necessary.
Evidence boundary
Improved reconstruction or calibration does not establish that downstream biological or treatment-effect conclusions are unbiased.
Editorial placement
Calibration, missing-data handling, privacy, and bias analysis support reliable wearable measurements and models; these methods do not themselves achieve a clinical endpoint.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

tsfresh

2018 · Canonical project documentation · infrastructure · Enabler · Tools, platforms & evaluation

Original source · Code · Project

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Automated extraction and relevance filtering of large collections of time-series features.
Why it matters
Provides a strong non-neural baseline and interpretable feature construction for wearable signals.
Limitations
Large feature spaces can overfit without participant-level splits, correction and external validation.
Evidence boundary
Tool inclusion documents available research infrastructure; it does not validate downstream scientific, causal or clinical claims.
Editorial placement
Acquisition, processing, software, or benchmark infrastructure supports sensing and modelling; a tool or platform is not itself a predictive, causal, or digital-twin result.
