Accepted registry record

Wearable Sensors for Parkinson’s Disease: Which Data Are Worth Collecting for Training Symptom Detection Models

2018 · npj Digital Medicine · measure · Enabler · Disease risk & digital biomarkers

Biomarkers · Disease risk

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Examines how sensor number, placement, participant diversity and repeated assessments affect tremor and bradykinesia detection.
Why it matters
Directly informs efficient study design and shows that more sensors or repeated sessions from the same people do not necessarily improve generalization.
Limitations
The cohort was small and clinic-task data may not represent free-living symptoms or longer-term progression.
Evidence boundary
This supports analytical or clinical validation in the studied cohort and device setting; it does not establish universal cross-device validity or downstream clinical benefit.
Editorial placement
Digital measures, longitudinal descriptions, or observational associations support the prediction route; an association is not a treatment effect or a calibrated individual future simulator.

Accepted registry record

Autocalibration of Accelerometer Data for Free-Living Physical Activity Assessment Using Local Gravity and Temperature

2014 · Journal of Applied Physiology · method · Enabler · Signal quality & trustworthy models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Uses local gravity and temperature information to reduce device calibration error in free-living accelerometry.
Why it matters
Addresses non-wear, irregular observation, device error and missingness mechanisms that otherwise contaminate wearable phenotypes and downstream causal analyses.
Limitations
Imputation or calibration can conceal non-random missingness and device-specific failure; uncertainty and sensitivity analyses remain necessary.
Evidence boundary
Improved reconstruction or calibration does not establish that downstream biological or treatment-effect conclusions are unbiased.
Editorial placement
Calibration, missing-data handling, privacy, and bias analysis support reliable wearable measurements and models; these methods do not themselves achieve a clinical endpoint.

2014 · Canonical project documentation · infrastructure · Enabler · Tools, platforms & evaluation

Original source · Code · Project

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Open-source R package for processing multi-day raw accelerometer data, including calibration, non-wear handling and sleep/activity summaries.
Why it matters
Widely used in population-scale wrist-accelerometry studies and provides reproducible end-to-end processing.
Limitations
Output validity depends on device metadata, calibration quality, parameter choices and phenotype definitions.
Evidence boundary
Tool inclusion documents available research infrastructure; it does not validate downstream scientific, causal or clinical claims.
Editorial placement
Acquisition, processing, software, or benchmark infrastructure supports sensing and modelling; a tool or platform is not itself a predictive, causal, or digital-twin result.

Accepted registry record

HL7 FHIR

2014 · HL7 International · infrastructure · Enabler · Personal-data infrastructure

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Defines a widely adopted standard for exchanging electronic health information through modular resources and APIs.
Why it matters
Wearable observations often need to enter clinical systems through interoperable data models.
Limitations
FHIR does not by itself harmonize sensor algorithms, sampling protocols or phenotype validity.
Evidence boundary
This resource defines a standard, governance or reporting framework. Conformance does not by itself demonstrate safety, effectiveness or clinical utility.
Editorial placement
Data collection, integration, or application infrastructure enables longitudinal personal systems; it is not evidence of a disease predictor or an implemented twin.

Accepted registry record

Multiple Imputation Using Chained Equations: Issues and Guidance for Practice

2011 · Statistics in Medicine · method · Enabler · Signal quality & trustworthy models

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Provides practical guidance for chained-equation multiple imputation under complex missing-data patterns.
Why it matters
Addresses non-wear, irregular observation, device error and missingness mechanisms that otherwise contaminate wearable phenotypes and downstream causal analyses.
Limitations
Imputation or calibration can conceal non-random missingness and device-specific failure; uncertainty and sensitivity analyses remain necessary.
Evidence boundary
Improved reconstruction or calibration does not establish that downstream biological or treatment-effect conclusions are unbiased.
Editorial placement
Calibration, missing-data handling, privacy, and bias analysis support reliable wearable measurements and models; these methods do not themselves achieve a clinical endpoint.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

A Digital Platform with Activity Tracking for Energy Management Support in Long COVID: A Randomised Controlled Trial

2026 · Nature Communications · intervention · Research · Adaptive health interventions

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Evaluates wearable activity tracking with threshold-triggered energy-management messages for adults with long COVID.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
The intervention was not more effective than control for post-exertional malaise or the primary endpoint.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary

A Randomized Trial of a Digitally Delivered, Home-Based Neuromodulation and Mindfulness Intervention for Pain Management in Older Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis

2026 · npj Digital Medicine · intervention · Adjacent · Neurostimulation & rehabilitation

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Tests remotely supervised home transcranial direct-current stimulation and mindfulness in a double-blind factorial trial.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
The combined intervention was not superior to active stimulation alone and benefits were not sustained at three months.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports the specified trial estimand, but it does not validate every algorithmic component, subgroup policy or future deployment configuration.
Editorial placement
Neural stimulation or rehabilitation studies inform sensing-linked intervention, but implanted or body-sensed clinical systems are adjacent to consumer wearable AI and need separate scope labels.
Review note
Source scope: body-sensed-adjacent; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

An Umbrella Review of Systematic Reviews of the Impact of Wrist-Worn Wearables on Health Outcomes

2026 · Physiological Reviews · intervention · Enabler · Intervention evidence synthesis

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Synthesizes 39 systematic reviews covering 98 primary studies of wrist-worn wearable feedback across physical activity, cardiometabolic, quality-of-life, mental-health and pain outcomes.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
Physical-activity benefits were more consistent; evidence for many other outcomes was limited or inconsistent and most reviews were rated low confidence.
Limitations
Conclusions inherit heterogeneity and risk of bias from included studies; devices, co-interventions, comparators and outcome definitions vary substantially.
Evidence boundary
Evidence synthesis estimates average effects over included studies and does not establish effectiveness for every device, population or intervention design.
Editorial placement
Reviews synthesize intervention outcomes and limitations; they are evidence resources, not new implemented algorithms or primary intervention trials.

Accepted registry record

Just-in-Time Adaptive Interventions: Where Are We Now and What Is Next?

2026 · Annual Review of Psychology · method · Framework · Adaptive-intervention synthesis

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Synthesizes the scientific rationale, current evidence and unresolved engagement, burden and social-context challenges in JITAI development.
Why it matters
Provides experimental designs and estimators for learning when, where and for whom wearable-triggered intervention components have proximal effects.
Limitations
Proximal effects may not translate into sustained clinical outcomes; burden, availability, habituation, interference and missing sensor data require explicit handling.
Evidence boundary
Micro-randomized evidence identifies randomized component effects at specified decision points, not the effectiveness of an untested full intervention package.
Editorial placement
Reviews the state and next steps of just-in-time adaptive interventions; the review is not itself a newly validated intervention policy.
Review note
Source scope: mobile-health-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

A Hybrid EMG–EEG Interface for Robust Intention Detection and Fatigue-Adaptive Control of an Elbow Rehabilitation Robot

2025 · Scientific Reports · model · Adjacent · Intention-aware rehabilitation control

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Combines peripheral EMG and central EEG to detect movement intention and adapt control when muscle fatigue degrades EMG-only recognition.
Why it matters
Illustrates multimodal wearable control that explicitly models a failure mode—fatigue—rather than assuming stationary sensor quality.
Limitations
The study is a technical evaluation with limited tasks and populations; it does not establish rehabilitation effectiveness, long-term safety or home deployment robustness.
Evidence boundary
This record supports a representation, recognition, sensing or control-system claim under the reported evaluation. It does not by itself establish clinical benefit, causal treatment effect, safety, transportability or regulatory readiness.
Editorial placement
Uses EMG and EEG intention detection to adapt an elbow rehabilitation controller under fatigue; this is an adjacent rehabilitation-control system, not an MR or personal-twin implementation.

An Adaptive AI-Based Virtual Reality Sports System for Adolescents with Excess Body Weight: A Randomized Controlled Trial

2025 · Nature Medicine · intervention · Research · VR-assisted health intervention

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Randomized five-arm evaluation of an adaptive VR sports system whose coaching agents were trained with deep reinforcement learning.
Why it matters
Connects adaptive AI policy learning to an embodied exercise intervention with a clinical body-composition endpoint.
Reported outcome
The adaptive VR sports arms reduced fat mass relative to control and were reported as comparable to physical sports over eight weeks.
Limitations
The eight-week trial involved adolescents with excess body weight in a structured VR setting; longer-term adherence, safety and transportability require study.
Evidence boundary
The reported effect is tied to the randomized intervention, comparator, population, follow-up and endpoint; it should not be generalized to other devices or care pathways without new evidence.
Editorial placement
Evaluates adaptive VR exercise in a randomized trial; VR is the intervention medium, not evidence of an MR-glasses personal-twin entry.
Review note
Source scope: body-sensed-adjacent; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Closed-Loop Vagus Nerve Stimulation Aids Recovery from Spinal Cord Injury

2025 · Nature · intervention · Adjacent · Neurostimulation & rehabilitation

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Double-blind sham-controlled randomized study paired successful sensor-measured rehabilitation movements with implanted vagus nerve stimulation.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence for a sensor-triggered implanted closed-loop rehabilitation system.
Reported outcome
Closed-loop stimulation paired with rehabilitation improved upper-limb strength and activities-of-daily-living measures relative to sham rehabilitation in the reported study.
Limitations
Early-feasibility study with 19 participants and an intensive specialized rehabilitation protocol; larger confirmatory trials are needed.
Evidence boundary
The reported effect is tied to the randomized intervention, comparator, population, follow-up and endpoint; it should not be generalized to other devices or care pathways without new evidence.
Editorial placement
Neural stimulation or rehabilitation studies inform sensing-linked intervention, but implanted or body-sensed clinical systems are adjacent to consumer wearable AI and need separate scope labels.

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Compares wrist-accelerometer and symptom monitoring with nurse-triggered escalation against surgeon-only perioperative care.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.

Effects of Physical Activity-Promoting Wearable Devices on Blood Pressure in Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

2025 · Hypertension Research · intervention · Enabler · Intervention evidence synthesis

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Synthesizes randomized trials of pedometers, activity trackers and smartwatches intended to improve blood pressure and related metabolic outcomes.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
The pooled evidence did not establish statistically significant improvements in blood pressure, weight, fasting glucose or HbA1c.
Limitations
Conclusions inherit heterogeneity and risk of bias from included studies; devices, co-interventions, comparators and outcome definitions vary substantially.
Evidence boundary
Evidence synthesis estimates average effects over included studies and does not establish effectiveness for every device, population or intervention design.
Editorial placement
Reviews synthesize intervention outcomes and limitations; they are evidence resources, not new implemented algorithms or primary intervention trials.

Contribution
Randomized trial compared six months of home telemedicine plus wearable monitoring and usual care with usual care alone for chronic musculoskeletal pain.
Why it matters
Adds longer-duration evidence for a wearable-enabled remote-care pathway rather than a short engagement study.
Reported outcome
No between-group pain difference was reported at one or three months; the telemedicine-plus-wearable group showed better outcomes at six months.
Limitations
Seventy-one participants, a bundled intervention and multiple outcomes limit attribution to the wearable component and broad generalization.
Evidence boundary
The reported effect is tied to the randomized intervention, comparator, population, follow-up and endpoint; it should not be generalized to other devices or care pathways without new evidence.
Editorial placement
The main contribution evaluates a therapeutic, rehabilitation, or assistive intervention; a personalized controller does not by itself establish a digital twin.

A Randomized Clinical Trial Testing Digital Mindset Intervention for Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Activity Improvement

2024 · npj Digital Medicine · intervention · Research · Rehabilitation & assistance

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Tests brief self-guided digital mindset and education interventions in adults with knee osteoarthritis.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
Mindset and self-reported physical activity improved relative to no intervention, while pain reduction was not significant.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports the specified trial estimand, but it does not validate every algorithmic component, subgroup policy or future deployment configuration.
Editorial placement
The main contribution evaluates a therapeutic, rehabilitation, or assistive intervention; a personalized controller does not by itself establish a digital twin.

2024 · Nature Communications · intervention · Research · Rehabilitation & assistance

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Multi-site randomized trial evaluated an autonomous closed-loop music system that adapts auditory stimulation to an individual's gait pattern.
Why it matters
Shows adaptive sensing and feedback improving a functional rehabilitation endpoint outside a laboratory-only demonstration.
Reported outcome
The intervention produced a larger improvement in walking speed and more clinical responders than active-control walking, with similar reported safety.
Limitations
The study evaluated chronic post-stroke walking over five weeks; generalization to other impairments and long-term maintenance requires evidence.

The reported effect is tied to the randomized intervention, comparator, population, follow-up and endpoint; it should not be generalized to other devices or care pathways without new evidence.

Accepted registry record

Interpretable Causal Inference for Analyzing Wearable, Sensor, and Distributional Data

2024 · AISTATS · method · Enabler · Causal identification

Causal inference

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Introduces ADD MALTS for interpretable matching and treatment-effect estimation when wearable outcomes are represented as distributions rather than scalar summaries.
Why it matters
Provides identification or estimation machinery needed before wearable associations can be interpreted as effects of actions or exposures.
Limitations
Validity depends on the stated causal graph, treatment definition, consistency, positivity, interference and confounding assumptions; flexible prediction alone does not remove these requirements.
Evidence boundary
This record supports causal methodology. It does not prove that any particular wearable-derived exposure or intervention has a causal effect without a design-specific analysis.
Editorial placement
Causal methodology supports reasoning about actions under explicit identification assumptions; generic methodological evidence does not establish the effect of a particular wearable intervention.

Accepted registry record

Longitudinal Targeted Minimum Loss-Based Estimation with Temporal-Difference Heterogeneous Transformer

2024 · ICML · method · Enabler · Longitudinal counterfactuals

Counterfactuals

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Combines a heterogeneous temporal transformer with longitudinal targeted learning to estimate dynamic-policy counterfactual means with confidence intervals.
Why it matters
Targets time-varying treatments and outcomes, which is closer to continuous wearable monitoring and adaptive health decisions than static treatment-effect estimation.
Limitations
Most evaluations use simulated or semi-synthetic counterfactuals; hidden confounding, treatment-policy shift, irregular sampling and weak overlap can invalidate estimates.
Evidence boundary
Counterfactual forecasts are conditional on identification and model assumptions and should not be presented as verified patient trajectories or clinical utility.
Editorial placement
Treatment-response estimation over time supports intervention reasoning; a conditional counterfactual model is not automatically a continuously updated individual digital twin.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Soft Robotic Apparel to Avert Freezing of Gait in Parkinson's Disease

2024 · Nature Medicine · intervention · Research · Rehabilitation & assistance

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Sensor-driven soft robotic garment delivered hip-flexion assistance and was evaluated through repeated assisted and unassisted walking in one person with Parkinson's disease.
Why it matters
Illustrates a genuine sensing–decision–actuation wearable loop targeting an acute motor impairment.
Reported outcome
Assistance eliminated freezing during the reported indoor tests for the single participant and improved walking distance and gait measures.
Limitations
N-of-1 proof of concept; efficacy, safety, usability and durability across patients are unknown.
Evidence boundary
Repeated within-person effects are compelling mechanistic evidence for this participant but cannot establish population-level effectiveness.
Editorial placement
The main contribution evaluates a therapeutic, rehabilitation, or assistive intervention; a personalized controller does not by itself establish a digital twin.

Accepted registry record

A Multi-Task Gaussian Process Model for Inferring Time-Varying Treatment Effects in Panel Data

2023 · AISTATS · method · Enabler · Longitudinal counterfactuals

Counterfactuals

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Uses structured Gaussian processes to infer dynamic counterfactual trajectories and uncertainty in treated and control panels.
Why it matters
Targets time-varying treatments and outcomes, which is closer to continuous wearable monitoring and adaptive health decisions than static treatment-effect estimation.
Limitations
Most evaluations use simulated or semi-synthetic counterfactuals; hidden confounding, treatment-policy shift, irregular sampling and weak overlap can invalidate estimates.
Evidence boundary
Counterfactual forecasts are conditional on identification and model assumptions and should not be presented as verified patient trajectories or clinical utility.
Editorial placement
Treatment-response estimation over time supports intervention reasoning; a conditional counterfactual model is not automatically a continuously updated individual digital twin.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

A Randomized Trial of a Mobile Health Intervention to Augment Cardiac Rehabilitation

2023 · npj Digital Medicine · intervention · Research · Adaptive health interventions

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Tests smartwatch-linked just-in-time text messaging as an adjunct to centre-based cardiac rehabilitation.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
The intervention did not improve the six-month primary outcome; limited device-specific secondary differences appeared earlier.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports the specified trial estimand, but it does not validate every algorithmic component, subgroup policy or future deployment configuration.
Editorial placement
The stated contribution evaluates an intervention or feedback pathway rather than only predicting a state; findings are limited to the tested intervention package and study population.

Walking Naturally after Spinal Cord Injury Using a Brain-Spine Interface

2023 · Nature · intervention · Adjacent · Neural rehabilitation control

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Links cortical decoding to spinal stimulation in a closed-loop brain-spine interface supporting walking after spinal-cord injury.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
Evidence comes from a highly specialized implanted system and a very small number of participants; scalability and durability remain unresolved.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports the specified trial estimand, but it does not validate every algorithmic component, subgroup policy or future deployment configuration.
Editorial placement
Links cortical decoding to spinal stimulation for walking assistance; an implanted clinical neural interface is adjacent to wearable AI and does not demonstrate an MR or personal-twin entry.
Review note
Do not infer randomization or population-level benefit from generic intervention boilerplate.

Accepted registry record

Wearable Technology Interventions in Patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

2023 · npj Digital Medicine · intervention · Enabler · Intervention evidence synthesis

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Evaluates wearable-supported activity and rehabilitation interventions in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
Meta-analysis reported increased step count, but study heterogeneity, attrition and per-protocol analyses limit certainty for broader clinical outcomes.
Limitations
Conclusions inherit heterogeneity and risk of bias from included studies; devices, co-interventions, comparators and outcome definitions vary substantially.
Evidence boundary
Evidence synthesis estimates average effects over included studies and does not establish effectiveness for every device, population or intervention design.
Editorial placement
Reviews synthesize intervention outcomes and limitations; they are evidence resources, not new implemented algorithms or primary intervention trials.

Effectiveness of Wearable Activity Trackers to Increase Physical Activity and Improve Health: A Systematic Review of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses

2022 · The Lancet Digital Health · intervention · Enabler · Intervention evidence synthesis

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Synthesizes systematic reviews and meta-analyses of activity-tracker interventions across clinical and non-clinical populations.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
Average physical activity, body composition and fitness improved, while several physiological and psychosocial outcomes were smaller or non-significant.
Limitations
Conclusions inherit heterogeneity and risk of bias from included studies; devices, co-interventions, comparators and outcome definitions vary substantially.
Evidence boundary
Evidence synthesis estimates average effects over included studies and does not establish effectiveness for every device, population or intervention design.
Editorial placement
Reviews synthesize intervention outcomes and limitations; they are evidence resources, not new implemented algorithms or primary intervention trials.

Accepted registry record

Multicenter, Randomized Trial of a Bionic Pancreas in Type 1 Diabetes

2022 · New England Journal of Medicine · intervention · Research · Closed-loop physiological control

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Tests an insulin-only bionic-pancreas system across age groups and multiple centres.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
Results concern a defined device ecosystem and clinical support model; long-term comparative effectiveness requires continuing surveillance.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports the specified trial estimand, but it does not validate every algorithmic component, subgroup policy or future deployment configuration.
Editorial placement
Sensing-linked physiological control or stimulation is the main contribution; closed-loop operation alone does not imply an individual digital twin or unrestricted counterfactual validity.

Accepted registry record

Predicting the Impact of Treatments over Time with Uncertainty-Aware Neural Differential Equations

2022 · AISTATS · method · Enabler · Longitudinal counterfactuals

Counterfactuals · Dynamic simulation

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Combines neural differential equations with uncertainty estimation to flag poorly supported longitudinal counterfactual predictions.
Why it matters
Targets time-varying treatments and outcomes, which is closer to continuous wearable monitoring and adaptive health decisions than static treatment-effect estimation.
Limitations
Most evaluations use simulated or semi-synthetic counterfactuals; hidden confounding, treatment-policy shift, irregular sampling and weak overlap can invalidate estimates.
Evidence boundary
Counterfactual forecasts are conditional on identification and model assumptions and should not be presented as verified patient trajectories or clinical utility.
Editorial placement
Treatment-response estimation over time supports intervention reasoning; a conditional counterfactual model is not automatically a continuously updated individual digital twin.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Smartphone-Based Screening for Atrial Fibrillation: A Pragmatic Randomized Clinical Trial

2022 · Nature Medicine · intervention · Research · Adaptive health interventions

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Pragmatic siteless randomized trial comparing smartphone pulse-wave screening plus confirmatory ECG with usual care in 5,551 adults.
Why it matters
Demonstrates that a digital sensing-to-confirmation pathway can change detection of treatment-relevant atrial fibrillation at population scale.
Reported outcome
Digital screening more than doubled detection of treatment-relevant atrial fibrillation in both trial phases.
Limitations
The sensing modality was smartphone photoplethysmography rather than a continuously worn device, and improved detection was not evidence of improved downstream clinical outcomes.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports an effect on AF detection under this screening pathway; it does not establish stroke reduction, net benefit or effectiveness of all wearable AF-screening strategies.
Editorial placement
The stated contribution evaluates an intervention or feedback pathway rather than only predicting a state; findings are limited to the tested intervention package and study population.
Review note
Source scope: mobile-health-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

The Micro-Randomized Trial for Developing Digital Interventions: Experimental Design and Data Analysis Considerations

2022 · Psychological Methods · method · Enabler · Adaptive trials & JITAI

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Consolidates practical design, availability, outcome-window and analysis considerations for modern micro-randomized trials.
Why it matters
Provides experimental designs and estimators for learning when, where and for whom wearable-triggered intervention components have proximal effects.
Limitations
Proximal effects may not translate into sustained clinical outcomes; burden, availability, habituation, interference and missing sensor data require explicit handling.
Evidence boundary
Micro-randomized evidence identifies randomized component effects at specified decision points, not the effectiveness of an untested full intervention package.
Editorial placement
Micro-randomized designs and estimators support evaluation of time-varying intervention effects; a design paper alone does not establish an effective deployed intervention.
Review note
Source scope: mobile-health-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Adaptive Deep Brain Stimulation in Advanced Parkinson Disease

2021 · Nature Medicine · intervention · Adjacent · Neurostimulation & rehabilitation

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Evaluates adaptive deep-brain stimulation driven by neural biomarkers in people with advanced Parkinson disease.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
Small specialized cohorts and invasive sensing constrain generalization; biomarker drift and long-term programming remain important.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports the specified trial estimand, but it does not validate every algorithmic component, subgroup policy or future deployment configuration.
Editorial placement
Neural stimulation or rehabilitation studies inform sensing-linked intervention, but implanted or body-sensed clinical systems are adjacent to consumer wearable AI and need separate scope labels.

Closed-Loop Neuromodulation in an Individual with Treatment-Resistant Depression

2021 · Nature Medicine · intervention · Adjacent · Individual closed-loop neurostimulation

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Demonstrates individualized biomarker-triggered intracranial stimulation for treatment-resistant depression in a single participant.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
This is an intensive single-participant demonstration and provides no population-level effectiveness estimate.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports the specified trial estimand, but it does not validate every algorithmic component, subgroup policy or future deployment configuration.
Editorial placement
Demonstrates biomarker-triggered intracranial stimulation in one participant; individualized closed-loop control is not a personal digital twin or a population-level randomized result.
Review note
Single-participant implanted clinical system; preserve its study-specific evidence boundary.

Effect of Wearing a Novel Electronic Wearable Device on Hand Hygiene Compliance Among Health Care Workers: A Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial

2021 · JAMA Network Open · intervention · Research · Adaptive health interventions

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial tested real-time wearable feedback on hand-rub duration and volume among healthcare workers.
Why it matters
Provides a useful negative example showing that sensor feedback can improve action quality without improving the intended behavioural frequency.
Reported outcome
The device did not improve compliance with hand-hygiene moments, although hand-rub volume and duration improved.
Limitations
Single geriatric hospital, volunteer wearers and strong time/Hawthorne effects complicate transportability.
Evidence boundary
The reported effect is tied to the randomized intervention, comparator, population, follow-up and endpoint; it should not be generalized to other devices or care pathways without new evidence.
Editorial placement
The stated contribution evaluates an intervention or feedback pathway rather than only predicting a state; findings are limited to the tested intervention package and study population.

Randomized Trial of Two Artificial Intelligence Coaching Interventions to Increase Physical Activity in Cancer Survivors

2021 · npj Digital Medicine · intervention · Research · Adaptive health interventions

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Three-arm pilot randomized trial comparing voice-assisted AI coaching, autonomous text coaching and health information, with Fitbit-derived steps as the primary outcome.
Why it matters
Provides direct randomized evidence for an AI coaching system informed by wearable activity data.
Reported outcome
Voice-assisted coaching increased steps relative to control over four weeks; the autonomous text arm did not show the same clear advantage.
Limitations
Single-center pilot with 42 participants, four weeks of intervention and a selected cancer-survivor population; durability and generalizability remain uncertain.
Evidence boundary
The reported effect is tied to the randomized intervention, comparator, population, follow-up and endpoint; it should not be generalized to other devices or care pathways without new evidence.
Editorial placement
The stated contribution evaluates an intervention or feedback pathway rather than only predicting a state; findings are limited to the tested intervention package and study population.

Accepted registry record

SyncTwin: Treatment Effect Estimation with Longitudinal Outcomes

2021 · NeurIPS · method · Enabler · Longitudinal counterfactuals

Counterfactuals · Dynamic simulation

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Constructs interpretable synthetic twins from pre-treatment longitudinal trajectories to estimate post-treatment counterfactual outcomes.
Why it matters
Targets time-varying treatments and outcomes, which is closer to continuous wearable monitoring and adaptive health decisions than static treatment-effect estimation.
Limitations
Most evaluations use simulated or semi-synthetic counterfactuals; hidden confounding, treatment-policy shift, irregular sampling and weak overlap can invalidate estimates.
Evidence boundary
Counterfactual forecasts are conditional on identification and model assumptions and should not be presented as verified patient trajectories or clinical utility.
Editorial placement
Constructs synthetic comparison units to estimate longitudinal treatment effects; the name SyncTwin does not mean a persistent person-specific physiological digital twin.
Review note
Synthetic-control twin is a methodological enabler, not an implemented personal twin. Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Algorithmic Recourse under Imperfect Causal Knowledge: A Probabilistic Approach

2020 · NeurIPS · method · Enabler · Predictive recourse

Counterfactuals

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Models uncertainty over causal structure when estimating whether recommended interventions will achieve algorithmic recourse.
Why it matters
Makes model decisions inspectable and helps distinguish an actionable change from a merely correlational perturbation of sensor features.
Limitations
Feasible feature changes may be biologically impossible, unsafe or non-causal; generated recourse can fail under model updates and population shift.
Evidence boundary
These are predictive or algorithmic counterfactuals unless a causal intervention model is explicitly identified and validated.
Editorial placement
Classifier recourse describes changes that alter a model prediction; such predictive counterfactuals must not be presented as verified causal treatment effects.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Causal Inference and Counterfactual Prediction in Machine Learning for Actionable Healthcare

2020 · Nature Machine Intelligence · method · Framework · Causal actionability framework

Causal frameworks · Causal inference

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Clarifies why accurate health prediction is insufficient for choosing actions and organizes causal and counterfactual requirements for actionable machine learning.
Why it matters
Provides identification or estimation machinery needed before wearable associations can be interpreted as effects of actions or exposures.
Limitations
Validity depends on the stated causal graph, treatment definition, consistency, positivity, interference and confounding assumptions; flexible prediction alone does not remove these requirements.
Evidence boundary
This record supports causal methodology. It does not prove that any particular wearable-derived exposure or intervention has a causal effect without a design-specific analysis.
Editorial placement
Organizes the causal and counterfactual requirements for actionable healthcare; it is a methodological framework rather than proof of a particular wearable intervention's effect.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

DYNOTEARS: Structure Learning from Time-Series Data

2020 · AISTATS · method · Enabler · Causal identification

Causal inference

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Extends continuous DAG optimization to contemporaneous and lagged dependencies in multivariate time series.
Why it matters
Supports hypothesis generation about temporal direction, invariance and latent structure in dense sensor streams when randomized interventions are unavailable.
Limitations
Causal discovery is sensitive to unmeasured confounding, measurement error, aggregation, sampling frequency, nonstationarity and violations of structural assumptions.
Evidence boundary
Recovered graphs or directions are hypotheses under assumptions; they are not automatically intervention-valid causal effects.
Editorial placement
Causal methodology supports reasoning about actions under explicit identification assumptions; generic methodological evidence does not establish the effect of a particular wearable intervention.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Estimating Counterfactual Treatment Outcomes over Time Through Adversarially Balanced Representations

2020 · ICLR · method · Enabler · Longitudinal counterfactuals

Counterfactuals

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Introduces Counterfactual Recurrent Networks with treatment-invariant temporal representations for multi-step treatment-response estimation.
Why it matters
Targets time-varying treatments and outcomes, which is closer to continuous wearable monitoring and adaptive health decisions than static treatment-effect estimation.
Limitations
Most evaluations use simulated or semi-synthetic counterfactuals; hidden confounding, treatment-policy shift, irregular sampling and weak overlap can invalidate estimates.
Evidence boundary
Counterfactual forecasts are conditional on identification and model assumptions and should not be presented as verified patient trajectories or clinical utility.
Editorial placement
Treatment-response estimation over time supports intervention reasoning; a conditional counterfactual model is not automatically a continuously updated individual digital twin.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Explaining Machine Learning Classifiers through Diverse Counterfactual Explanations

2020 · FAccT · method · Enabler · Predictive recourse

Counterfactuals

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Introduces DiCE to generate diverse counterfactual examples that expose alternative feature configurations changing a classifier prediction.
Why it matters
Makes model decisions inspectable and helps distinguish an actionable change from a merely correlational perturbation of sensor features.
Limitations
Feasible feature changes may be biologically impossible, unsafe or non-causal; generated recourse can fail under model updates and population shift.
Evidence boundary
These are predictive or algorithmic counterfactuals unless a causal intervention model is explicitly identified and validated.
Editorial placement
Classifier recourse describes changes that alter a model prediction; such predictive counterfactuals must not be presented as verified causal treatment effects.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Gradient Regularized V-Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes

2020 · NeurIPS · method · Enabler · Policy learning & evaluation

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Uses gradient regularization and value learning to estimate non-Markovian dynamic treatment regimes.
Why it matters
Provides a formal route from repeated sensing to sequential treatment or intervention policies rather than one-time risk prediction.
Limitations
Estimated policies can be unstable under limited overlap, misspecified rewards, delayed outcomes, nonstationarity, safety constraints and distribution shift.
Evidence boundary
Policy-learning performance in retrospective or simulated data does not establish prospective clinical benefit or safe deployment.
Editorial placement
Policy learning or off-policy evaluation supports sequential decisions under study-specific assumptions; a generic algorithm is not a prospectively validated wearable intervention.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Guidelines for Clinical Trial Protocols for Interventions Involving Artificial Intelligence: The SPIRIT-AI Extension

2020 · Nature Medicine · infrastructure · Enabler · Trial reporting & validation

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Extends SPIRIT for protocols evaluating interventions that include an AI component.
Why it matters
Makes planned AI inputs, outputs, human-AI interactions and error handling explicit before a trial is run.
Limitations
Protocol reporting cannot compensate for an inappropriate comparator, endpoint or deployment context.
Evidence boundary
This is protocol-reporting guidance, not effectiveness evidence.

Protocol-reporting guidance supports AI intervention study design; a guideline does not demonstrate predictive, causal, or twin capability.

Nine-Year Prospective Efficacy and Safety of Brain-Responsive Neurostimulation for Focal Epilepsy

2020 · Neurology · intervention · Adjacent · Neurostimulation & rehabilitation

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Reports long-term prospective effectiveness and safety of responsive neurostimulation for focal epilepsy.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
Long-term observational follow-up is vulnerable to attrition, changing management and survivor effects despite its deployment relevance.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports the specified trial estimand, but it does not validate every algorithmic component, subgroup policy or future deployment configuration.
Editorial placement
Neural stimulation or rehabilitation studies inform sensing-linked intervention, but implanted or body-sensed clinical systems are adjacent to consumer wearable AI and need separate scope labels.

Reporting Guidelines for Clinical Trial Reports for Interventions Involving Artificial Intelligence: The CONSORT-AI Extension

2020 · Nature Medicine · infrastructure · Enabler · Trial reporting & validation

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Extends CONSORT reporting requirements for randomized evaluations of AI interventions.
Why it matters
Improves transparency about inputs, outputs, human interaction, errors and AI-specific trial conduct.
Limitations
Reporting completeness does not correct design bias or guarantee generalizability.
Evidence boundary
A reporting guideline does not establish intervention effectiveness.
Editorial placement
Reporting guidance for AI intervention trials constrains evaluation claims; it is not an implemented intervention or new treatment-effect result.

Accepted registry record

Time Series Deconfounder: Estimating Treatment Effects over Time in the Presence of Hidden Confounders

2020 · ICML · method · Enabler · Longitudinal counterfactuals

Counterfactuals

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Uses multi-treatment temporal factor modelling to construct substitute confounders before longitudinal treatment-effect estimation.
Why it matters
Targets time-varying treatments and outcomes, which is closer to continuous wearable monitoring and adaptive health decisions than static treatment-effect estimation.
Limitations
Most evaluations use simulated or semi-synthetic counterfactuals; hidden confounding, treatment-policy shift, irregular sampling and weak overlap can invalidate estimates.
Evidence boundary
Counterfactual forecasts are conditional on identification and model assumptions and should not be presented as verified patient trajectories or clinical utility.
Editorial placement
Treatment-response estimation over time supports intervention reasoning; a conditional counterfactual model is not automatically a continuously updated individual digital twin.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Variational Autoencoders and Nonlinear ICA: A Unifying Framework

2020 · AISTATS · method · Enabler · Causal identification

Causal inference

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Provides identifiability conditions for nonlinear latent components using auxiliary variables, relevant to disentangling latent physiological states.
Why it matters
Supports hypothesis generation about temporal direction, invariance and latent structure in dense sensor streams when randomized interventions are unavailable.
Limitations
Causal discovery is sensitive to unmeasured confounding, measurement error, aggregation, sampling frequency, nonstationarity and violations of structural assumptions.
Evidence boundary
Recovered graphs or directions are hypotheses under assumptions; they are not automatically intervention-valid causal effects.
Editorial placement
Causal methodology supports reasoning about actions under explicit identification assumptions; generic methodological evidence does not establish the effect of a particular wearable intervention.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Adapting Neural Networks for the Estimation of Treatment Effects

2019 · NeurIPS · method · Enabler · Causal identification

Causal inference

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Introduces Dragonnet and targeted regularization to align representation learning with treatment-effect estimation.
Why it matters
Provides identification or estimation machinery needed before wearable associations can be interpreted as effects of actions or exposures.
Limitations
Validity depends on the stated causal graph, treatment definition, consistency, positivity, interference and confounding assumptions; flexible prediction alone does not remove these requirements.
Evidence boundary
This record supports causal methodology. It does not prove that any particular wearable-derived exposure or intervention has a causal effect without a design-specific analysis.
Editorial placement
Causal methodology supports reasoning about actions under explicit identification assumptions; generic methodological evidence does not establish the effect of a particular wearable intervention.

Efficacy of Contextually Tailored Suggestions for Physical Activity: A Micro-Randomized Optimization Trial of HeartSteps

2019 · Annals of Behavioral Medicine · method · Research · Adaptive trials & JITAI

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Applies repeated randomization to estimate the short-term effect of contextually tailored walking and anti-sedentary suggestions.
Why it matters
Provides experimental designs and estimators for learning when, where and for whom wearable-triggered intervention components have proximal effects.
Limitations
Proximal effects may not translate into sustained clinical outcomes; burden, availability, habituation, interference and missing sensor data require explicit handling.
Evidence boundary
Micro-randomized evidence identifies randomized component effects at specified decision points, not the effectiveness of an untested full intervention package.
Editorial placement
Tests the effects of contextually tailored activity suggestions in a micro-randomized optimization trial; it evaluates an intervention, rather than only proposing a trial design.

2019 · Annals of Statistics · method · Enabler · Causal identification

Causal inference

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Generalizes forest-based local moment estimation to treatment effects, instrumental variables and other heterogeneous estimands.
Why it matters
Provides identification or estimation machinery needed before wearable associations can be interpreted as effects of actions or exposures.
Limitations
Validity depends on the stated causal graph, treatment definition, consistency, positivity, interference and confounding assumptions; flexible prediction alone does not remove these requirements.
Evidence boundary
This record supports causal methodology. It does not prove that any particular wearable-derived exposure or intervention has a causal effect without a design-specific analysis.
Editorial placement
Causal methodology supports reasoning about actions under explicit identification assumptions; generic methodological evidence does not establish the effect of a particular wearable intervention.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Gradient-Based Neural DAG Learning

2019 · NeurIPS · method · Enabler · Causal identification

Causal inference

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Learns nonlinear causal graphs through gradient-based optimization of neural structural equations.
Why it matters
Supports hypothesis generation about temporal direction, invariance and latent structure in dense sensor streams when randomized interventions are unavailable.
Limitations
Causal discovery is sensitive to unmeasured confounding, measurement error, aggregation, sampling frequency, nonstationarity and violations of structural assumptions.
Evidence boundary
Recovered graphs or directions are hypotheses under assumptions; they are not automatically intervention-valid causal effects.
Editorial placement
Causal methodology supports reasoning about actions under explicit identification assumptions; generic methodological evidence does not establish the effect of a particular wearable intervention.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Guidelines for Reinforcement Learning in Healthcare

2019 · Nature Medicine · method · Enabler · Policy learning & evaluation

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Specifies design, evaluation and reporting hazards for reinforcement learning in clinical settings, including confounding, reward design and unsafe recommendations.
Why it matters
Allows proposed adaptive policies to be screened using logged data before expensive or unsafe online deployment.
Limitations
Reliable evaluation requires known or estimable behavior policies, adequate support, correct nuisance models and careful uncertainty analysis.
Evidence boundary
Off-policy value is an estimate under assumptions and does not replace prospective randomized evaluation for high-stakes health systems.
Editorial placement
Policy learning or off-policy evaluation supports sequential decisions under study-specific assumptions; a generic algorithm is not a prospectively validated wearable intervention.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Six-Month Randomized, Multicenter Trial of Closed-Loop Control in Type 1 Diabetes

2019 · New England Journal of Medicine · intervention · Research · Closed-loop physiological control

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Evaluates a closed-loop insulin-delivery system over six months across multiple clinical centres.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
Clinical benefit and adverse-event profiles remain system-, training- and population-specific.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports the specified trial estimand, but it does not validate every algorithmic component, subgroup policy or future deployment configuration.
Editorial placement
Sensing-linked physiological control or stimulation is the main contribution; closed-loop operation alone does not imply an individual digital twin or unrestricted counterfactual validity.

Accepted registry record

Assessing Time-Varying Causal Effect Moderation in Mobile Health

2018 · Journal of the American Statistical Association · method · Enabler · Adaptive trials & JITAI

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Provides weighted and centered estimation for time-varying proximal causal effects and moderators in micro-randomized trials.
Why it matters
Provides experimental designs and estimators for learning when, where and for whom wearable-triggered intervention components have proximal effects.
Limitations
Proximal effects may not translate into sustained clinical outcomes; burden, availability, habituation, interference and missing sensor data require explicit handling.
Evidence boundary
Micro-randomized evidence identifies randomized component effects at specified decision points, not the effectiveness of an untested full intervention package.
Editorial placement
Micro-randomized designs and estimators support evaluation of time-varying intervention effects; a design paper alone does not establish an effective deployed intervention.
Review note
Source scope: mobile-health-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Forecasting Treatment Responses Over Time Using Recurrent Marginal Structural Networks

2018 · NeurIPS · method · Enabler · Longitudinal counterfactuals

Counterfactuals · Dynamic simulation

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Builds recurrent marginal structural networks for forecasting responses to planned treatment sequences under time-dependent confounding.
Why it matters
Targets time-varying treatments and outcomes, which is closer to continuous wearable monitoring and adaptive health decisions than static treatment-effect estimation.
Limitations
Most evaluations use simulated or semi-synthetic counterfactuals; hidden confounding, treatment-policy shift, irregular sampling and weak overlap can invalidate estimates.
Evidence boundary
Counterfactual forecasts are conditional on identification and model assumptions and should not be presented as verified patient trajectories or clinical utility.
Editorial placement
Treatment-response estimation over time supports intervention reasoning; a conditional counterfactual model is not automatically a continuously updated individual digital twin.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

GANITE: Estimation of Individualized Treatment Effects Using Generative Adversarial Nets

2018 · ICLR · method · Enabler · Causal identification

Causal inference

Original source · Code

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Uses adversarial learning to impute counterfactual outcomes and estimate individualized treatment effects.
Why it matters
Provides identification or estimation machinery needed before wearable associations can be interpreted as effects of actions or exposures.
Limitations
Validity depends on the stated causal graph, treatment definition, consistency, positivity, interference and confounding assumptions; flexible prediction alone does not remove these requirements.
Evidence boundary
This record supports causal methodology. It does not prove that any particular wearable-derived exposure or intervention has a causal effect without a design-specific analysis.
Editorial placement
Causal methodology supports reasoning about actions under explicit identification assumptions; generic methodological evidence does not establish the effect of a particular wearable intervention.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Sample Size Calculations for Micro-Randomized Trials in mHealth

2018 · Statistics in Medicine · method · Enabler · Adaptive trials & JITAI

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Provides power and sample-size calculations for proximal treatment effects under repeated randomization.
Why it matters
Provides experimental designs and estimators for learning when, where and for whom wearable-triggered intervention components have proximal effects.
Limitations
Proximal effects may not translate into sustained clinical outcomes; burden, availability, habituation, interference and missing sensor data require explicit handling.
Evidence boundary
Micro-randomized evidence identifies randomized component effects at specified decision points, not the effectiveness of an untested full intervention package.
Editorial placement
Micro-randomized designs and estimators support evaluation of time-varying intervention effects; a design paper alone does not establish an effective deployed intervention.
Review note
Source scope: mobile-health-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

The Artificial Intelligence Clinician Learns Optimal Treatment Strategies for Sepsis in Intensive Care

2018 · Nature Medicine · method · Enabler · Policy learning & evaluation

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Demonstrates retrospective reinforcement-learning policy estimation for sequential sepsis treatment and illustrates both the promise and controversy of observational policy learning.
Why it matters
Provides a formal route from repeated sensing to sequential treatment or intervention policies rather than one-time risk prediction.
Limitations
Estimated policies can be unstable under limited overlap, misspecified rewards, delayed outcomes, nonstationarity, safety constraints and distribution shift.
Evidence boundary
Policy-learning performance in retrospective or simulated data does not establish prospective clinical benefit or safe deployment.
Editorial placement
Policy learning or off-policy evaluation supports sequential decisions under study-specific assumptions; a generic algorithm is not a prospectively validated wearable intervention.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Causal Inference Using Invariant Prediction: Identification and Confidence Intervals

2016 · Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B · method · Enabler · Causal identification

Causal inference

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Uses stability of conditional relationships across environments to identify plausible causal predictors and construct confidence sets.
Why it matters
Supports hypothesis generation about temporal direction, invariance and latent structure in dense sensor streams when randomized interventions are unavailable.
Limitations
Causal discovery is sensitive to unmeasured confounding, measurement error, aggregation, sampling frequency, nonstationarity and violations of structural assumptions.
Evidence boundary
Recovered graphs or directions are hypotheses under assumptions; they are not automatically intervention-valid causal effects.
Editorial placement
Causal methodology supports reasoning about actions under explicit identification assumptions; generic methodological evidence does not establish the effect of a particular wearable intervention.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Closed-Loop Insulin Delivery during Pregnancy in Women with Type 1 Diabetes

2016 · New England Journal of Medicine · intervention · Research · Closed-loop physiological control

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Evaluates closed-loop insulin delivery during pregnancy, a high-risk context with rapidly changing physiology.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
Small specialized samples and intensive support limit generalization beyond the tested pregnancy setting.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports the specified trial estimand, but it does not validate every algorithmic component, subgroup policy or future deployment configuration.
Editorial placement
Sensing-linked physiological control or stimulation is the main contribution; closed-loop operation alone does not imply an individual digital twin or unrestricted counterfactual validity.

Accepted registry record

Data-Efficient Off-Policy Policy Evaluation for Reinforcement Learning

2016 · ICML · method · Enabler · Policy learning & evaluation

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Develops high-confidence and data-efficient estimators for evaluating policies from logged trajectories.
Why it matters
Allows proposed adaptive policies to be screened using logged data before expensive or unsafe online deployment.
Limitations
Reliable evaluation requires known or estimable behavior policies, adequate support, correct nuisance models and careful uncertainty analysis.
Evidence boundary
Off-policy value is an estimate under assumptions and does not replace prospective randomized evaluation for high-stakes health systems.
Editorial placement
Policy learning or off-policy evaluation supports sequential decisions under study-specific assumptions; a generic algorithm is not a prospectively validated wearable intervention.
Review note
Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Effect of Wearable Technology Combined With a Lifestyle Intervention on Long-term Weight Loss: The IDEA Randomized Clinical Trial

2016 · JAMA · intervention · Research · Adaptive health interventions

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Tests adding a wearable activity monitor to a standard behavioral weight-loss intervention over 24 months.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
Adding the wearable component did not improve weight loss and the technology-enhanced arm lost less weight than the standard intervention arm.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports the specified trial estimand, but it does not validate every algorithmic component, subgroup policy or future deployment configuration.
Editorial placement
The stated contribution evaluates an intervention or feedback pathway rather than only predicting a state; findings are limited to the tested intervention package and study population.

Accepted registry record

Micro-Randomized Trials in mHealth

2016 · Statistics in Medicine · method · Enabler · Adaptive trials & JITAI

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Develops statistical principles for repeated-randomization mobile-health trials with time-varying availability and proximal outcomes.
Why it matters
Provides experimental designs and estimators for learning when, where and for whom wearable-triggered intervention components have proximal effects.
Limitations
Proximal effects may not translate into sustained clinical outcomes; burden, availability, habituation, interference and missing sensor data require explicit handling.
Evidence boundary
Micro-randomized evidence identifies randomized component effects at specified decision points, not the effectiveness of an untested full intervention package.
Editorial placement
Micro-randomized designs and estimators support evaluation of time-varying intervention effects; a design paper alone does not establish an effective deployed intervention.
Review note
Source scope: mobile-health-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

Home Use of an Artificial Beta Cell in Type 1 Diabetes

2015 · New England Journal of Medicine · intervention · Research · Closed-loop physiological control

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Tests extended home use of closed-loop insulin delivery compared with sensor-augmented pump therapy.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
Benefits apply to the evaluated algorithm, hardware and monitored population; failures, training and real-world adherence remain relevant.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports the specified trial estimand, but it does not validate every algorithmic component, subgroup policy or future deployment configuration.
Editorial placement
Sensing-linked physiological control or stimulation is the main contribution; closed-loop operation alone does not imply an individual digital twin or unrestricted counterfactual validity.

Accepted registry record

Microrandomized Trials: An Experimental Design for Developing Just-in-Time Adaptive Interventions

2015 · Health Psychology · method · Enabler · Adaptive trials & JITAI

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Defines the micro-randomized trial as repeated randomization at intervention decision points for estimating proximal component effects.
Why it matters
Provides experimental designs and estimators for learning when, where and for whom wearable-triggered intervention components have proximal effects.
Limitations
Proximal effects may not translate into sustained clinical outcomes; burden, availability, habituation, interference and missing sensor data require explicit handling.
Evidence boundary
Micro-randomized evidence identifies randomized component effects at specified decision points, not the effectiveness of an untested full intervention package.
Editorial placement
Micro-randomized designs and estimators support evaluation of time-varying intervention effects; a design paper alone does not establish an effective deployed intervention.
Review note
Source scope: mobile-health-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Accepted registry record

V-Learning for Dynamic Treatment Effects

2015 · Journal of the American Statistical Association · method · Enabler · Policy learning & evaluation

Adaptive interventions

Source link withheld: Title and DOI mismatch: DOI resolves to Zhao et al. dynamic-treatment-regime methods, not mHealth V-learning; link withheld.

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Estimates optimal dynamic treatment regimes through value-function learning without fully modelling outcome dynamics.
Why it matters
Provides a formal route from repeated sensing to sequential treatment or intervention policies rather than one-time risk prediction.
Limitations
Estimated policies can be unstable under limited overlap, misspecified rewards, delayed outcomes, nonstationarity, safety constraints and distribution shift.
Evidence boundary
Policy-learning performance in retrospective or simulated data does not establish prospective clinical benefit or safe deployment.
Editorial placement
Dynamic treatment-policy learning is a methodological enabler; source identity must be resolved before citing this particular registry entry as evidence.
Review note
Known source-link issue in the existing map; no canonical record is removed or rewritten by this classification. Source scope: cross-domain-enabler; relevance does not establish a consumer-wearable implementation.

Outpatient Glycemic Control with a Bionic Pancreas in Type 1 Diabetes

2014 · New England Journal of Medicine · intervention · Research · Closed-loop physiological control

Adaptive interventions

Original source

Contribution, evidence boundary & original metadata
Contribution
Evaluates bihormonal closed-loop insulin and glucagon delivery in outpatient adults and adolescents with type 1 diabetes.
Why it matters
Provides direct evidence about whether sensing-linked feedback, adaptive messaging, automated control or closed-loop stimulation changes behaviour, physiology or clinical outcomes.
Reported outcome
Short-duration crossover evidence supports glycemic control in the tested system; device complexity and long-term safety require separate evaluation.
Limitations
Effects are specific to the tested population, intervention package, comparator, device, adherence pattern and follow-up window; transportability and long-term safety require separate evidence.
Evidence boundary
Randomization supports the specified trial estimand, but it does not validate every algorithmic component, subgroup policy or future deployment configuration.
Editorial placement
Sensing-linked physiological control or stimulation is the main contribution; closed-loop operation alone does not imply an individual digital twin or unrestricted counterfactual validity.
